CVE-2026-82049: the tarfile module's data and tar extraction filters could be bypassed by an archive containing a hard link to a symbolic link, letting extraction change the permissions or modification time of a file outside the destination directory or expose that file's contents inside the extracted tree. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157190 with the 3.12 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/cc1689830c6b9aaddded2fb9f2fe8116867e2c0e, from https://github.com/python/cpython/pull/157454, which makes TarFile.makelink_with_filter() link to os.path.realpath() of the link target. It was first released in CPython 3.12.15: https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82049, https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/EFJWGAZJA56AKSBR2WHMHQZO7RRLZPRH/. Checked Lib/tarfile.py in the python-3.12 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.16-r4, on x86_64 and aarch64, for the fixed os.link(os.path.realpath(tarinfo._link_target)) call in makelink_with_filter(), a method present in every build; both architectures agree. 3.12.12-r0 to 3.12.14-r1 lack the fix (3.12.14-r1 ships the upstream 3.12.14 file unchanged). 3.12.14-r2 carries a backport, and its tarfile.py is byte-identical to the upstream 3.12.15 file; 3.12.15-r0 and later ship the upstream 3.12.15 or later file. The compiled tarfile .pyc files in python-3.12-pycache-pyc0, python-3.12-pycache-pyc1 and python-3.12-pycache-pyc2 are checked-hash .pyc files, which the interpreter validates against that source, and their source hash changes in step with it. The range ends at 3.12.14-r2, the first published build with the fix, so the upstream-version identifier python 3.12.14 reads as affected.

CVE-2026-82049: in CPython 3.13 and earlier, the tarfile module's 'data' and 'tar' extraction filters could be bypassed by an archive containing a hard link to a symbolic link: os.link() recreated the symlink itself at the hard link's location, where its relative target could point outside the destination directory, so extraction could change the permissions or modification time of a file outside the destination or expose that file's contents in the extracted tree. Upstream fixed it in https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157190 (3.13 commit https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/b8f23e307097552eaea2604383a12ab280520d0d, which resolves the link target with os.path.realpath() before calling os.link()), first released in CPython 3.13.16; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/EFJWGAZJA56AKSBR2WHMHQZO7RRLZPRH/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82049. Read Lib/tarfile.py in the python-3.13 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository, 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.18-r4 (26 builds), x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree, and each build's libpython3.13 carries the CPython release its version names. 3.13.12-r0 to 3.13.15-r1 pass the link target to os.link() unresolved. 3.13.15-r2, a CPython 3.13.15 build, carries a DHI backport of the upstream change (makelink_with_filter() calls os.link(os.path.realpath(...))), and every build from 3.13.16-r0 on ships the upstream CPython 3.13.16 or later file, which has the fix. The range ends at 3.13.15-r2.

CVE-2026-82049: in CPython 3.13 and earlier, tarfile's 'data' and 'tar' extraction filters could be bypassed by an archive containing a hard link to a symlink: os.link() recreated the symlink itself at the hard link's location, where its relative target could point outside the destination, so extraction could change the mode and modification time of an outside file or expose its contents. The CVE record lists CPython 3.14 as affected only before 3.14.0b1, and the upstream issue https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157190 says 3.14 was fixed incidentally by https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/5a57248b22ad3b9aafcaaadae2c304a1923daeca, which makes os.link() follow symlinks (linkat() with AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW) and was first released in 3.14.0b1; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/EFJWGAZJA56AKSBR2WHMHQZO7RRLZPRH/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82049. Every published build of the DHI Alpine 3.23 python-3.14 package, 3.14.3-r0 to 3.14.10-r4 on x86_64 and aarch64, is built from CPython 3.14.3 or later (the version string in libpython3.14.so), so every build has that change. Ran the interpreter from 3.14.3-r0, the lowest published build, and 3.14.7-r1 on arm64: os.link() on a symlink creates a hard link to its target, and extracting an archive of the shape in the upstream issue with the 'data' filter leaves a regular file with the in-tree contents; a DHI python-3.13 3.13.12 build run the same way leaves a symlink that reads the outside file. From 3.14.7-r2, builds also resolve the link target with os.path.realpath() before os.link(), a backport of the later upstream 3.14 hardening (https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/c66df4e70435d257fd488b35ea129c6f317433a8, released in 3.14.8) that the 3.14.10 builds ship unchanged. Every published build has the fix, so the range ends at the lowest published build, 3.14.3-r0.

CVE-2026-82049: in CPython 3.13 and earlier, tarfile's 'data' and 'tar' extraction filters could be bypassed by an archive containing a hard link to a symlink: os.link() recreated the symlink itself at the hard link's location, where its relative target could point outside the destination, so extraction could change the mode and modification time of an outside file or expose its contents. The CVE record lists no 3.15 release as affected (3.14 only before 3.14.0b1), and the upstream issue https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/157190 says 3.14 and later were fixed incidentally by https://github.com/python/cpython/commit/5a57248b22ad3b9aafcaaadae2c304a1923daeca, first released in 3.14.0b1, which makes os.link() call linkat() with AT_SYMLINK_FOLLOW so that a hard link to a symlink links its target; see https://mail.python.org/archives/list/security-announce@python.org/thread/EFJWGAZJA56AKSBR2WHMHQZO7RRLZPRH/ and https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-82049. The 3.15.0 and 3.15.2 sources of Modules/posixmodule.c have that change, and in every build named below the libpython3.15.so imports linkat(). Compared Lib/tarfile.py in the python-3.15 package of every build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-28 (3.15.0-r0 and 3.15.2-r0 to 3.15.2-r4), on x86_64 and aarch64 with the same file in the upstream CPython release of that build's version (each build is CPython 3.15.0 or 3.15.2 by the version string in its libpython3.15.so): every build ships the upstream file unchanged.
